p local-id

aee0a52c2984

This meeting focused on AI knowledge sharing a

nd progress updates across the project layers. Daijiang Xie introduced STOA

G

Self-Training On-Going Agent

, an enhanced RAG-agent approach that uses

a controller to determine whether the available evidence is sufficient and

to identify information gaps for targeted follow-up retrieval. The Data Pro

cessing Layer completed semantic segmentation and card-system development.

The Tool Layer tested an English financial QA dataset and explored re-ranki

ng and BM25 tokenization improvements, while identifying issues with recall

quality and chunking. The Integration Layer presented CPR-system enhanceme

nts, including multi-turn tool calling, short-term memory, and query rewrit

ing. The Monitoring Layer developed frontend observability features. The me

eting also confirmed that a document-listing function can be implemented se

curely through appropriate permission controls.

h3 local-id

MeetingMinutesof2026

27-Q2reporting-

STOAGKnowledgeSharing

STOAG Knowledge Sharing

p local-id

ea0dcbd46c60

Daijiang Xie shared STOAG, a solution designed

to improve Retrieval-Augmented Generation

agents in multi-hop questi

on-answering scenarios. Traditional RAG agents may stop retrieval too early

or continue searching unnecessarily. STOAG addresses this issue by introdu

cing a controller that evaluates whether the current evidence is sufficient

to answer the question.

p local-id

4135a4eac62e

The controller examines evidence sufficiency a

nd identifies missing information. If the available evidence is adequate, r

etrieval stops. Otherwise, the system generates structured information-gap

descriptions to guide the next retrieval round. Daijiang suggested integrat

ing this approach into the current project, potentially through the evidenc

e-context component.

h3 local-id

fb03b22aa7b7

MeetingMinutesof2026

27-Q2reporting-

IterativeRetrievalDiscussion

Iterative Retrieval Discussion

p local-id

2cf43da11290

Tao asked for an example of iterative retrieva

l. Daijiang explained that the approach progressively focuses on evidence m

issing from the previous retrieval round. Vincent asked about the specific

algorithm used by the judge controller

Daijiang noted that he would verify

the implementation details from the paper.

h3 local-id

fb320b4abc36

MeetingMinutesof2026

27-Q2reporting-

ConfluenceSecurityandWebLayerProgress

Confluence Security and Web Layer Pr

ogress

p local-id

eada964b223a

Guangyuan Mu reported that the Confluence work

space has been created and that some members have uploaded technical docume

nts. However, most members still need to upload their completed work.

p local-id

a7588f5920fb

Suijie Song introduced the Web Layer

task allocation, including API documentation and CPI-function planning. Co

mpleted features include string tabs, message persistence, and authenticati

on. Tao asked about the CPI plan and current progress

Suijie confirmed tha

t the related documentation is available in the shared folder.

h3 local-id

7cbc609eaf25

MeetingMinutesof2026

27-Q2reporting-

DataProcessingLayerDevelopment

Data Processing Layer Development

p local-id

8cf9bcc99359

Guangyuan Mu presented the Data Processing Lay

er

99s completed semantic segmentation and card-system functionality.

A pre-compressor was added to calculate text weights, remove low-value con

tent such as filler words, and use sentence similarity to create more natur

al semantic segments.

p local-id

54435dfcb3b0

After segmentation, the system groups sentence

s by topic using a hash-table structure. When content exceeds a defined thr

eshold, the system produces a summary and invokes an LLM to generate cards

containing key content and keywords.

p local-id

a74fd4732e68

Guangyuan also discussed link-type relationshi

ps, including conflict, evidence, and support relationships, as well as tim

estamp-based update mechanisms. Zeng Zhong

99s Confluence document-pa

rsing work was also mentioned.

h3 local-id

55437e03ba51

MeetingMinutesof2026

27-Q2reporting-

RankingandBM25Improvements

Ranking and BM25 Improvements

p local-id

22b08a99aa47

Jiaxing Dai reported progress on adding a rank

ing function and changing the BM25 tokenizer from Chinese to English. He te

sted the system using an English financial information-retrieval dataset co

ntaining 648 queries and 400 documents. The overall results were not yet sa

tisfactory.

p local-id

e5cef29f00ee

Vincent suggested exploring more flexible rank

ing approaches for document chunks. The team discussed retrieval-quality an

d embedding-segmentation issues. Vincent recommended testing higher-dimensi

onal embedding models, approximately 1,000

932,000 dimensions, and co

nsidering an A2 model. He also noted that reducing chunk dimensions below 8

could significantly weaken relevance.

h3 local-id

82cd88a34047

MeetingMinutesof2026

27-Q2reporting-

CPRSystemEnhancement

CPR System Enhancement

p local-id

05678b59201f

Daijiang introduced CPR-system enhancements, i

ncluding multi-turn execution and short-term memory, enabling the model to

ask follow-up questions and retain conversational context.

p local-id

4beed277de44

Huifang Liu presented the main user-request-pr

ocessing components

intent classification, coreference resolution, and que

ry rewriting. Seven question categories have been completed.

p local-id

510ed965f560

The Monitoring Layer also demonstrated fronten

d observability features, including real-time requests-per-second and P95-l

atency monitoring, as well as automated API-metric collection. The team dis

cussed confidentiality concerns around the document management system and a

greed that the document-listing feature can be safely supported through acc

ess-control mechanisms.

p local-id

4bd8db74076e

The team will complete remaining layer-level i

mprovements and prepare for integration testing next week.

p local-id
